changes: Year reinterpreted: 'sataddevatsare pūrṇṇa paścāvaśām ekādhike' is most likely a corrupt 'śatadve vatsare pūrṇe pañcāśad ekādhike' = 200 + 51 = 251, not 200 as the catalogue says. ce_approx changed from 1080 to 1131 accordingly; marked uncertain.
Era set to NS (assumed; not stated in the colophon) instead of 'unspecified', so that ce_approx can be given.
Month normalised to Āṣāḍha; tithi to daśamī; nakṣatra to Viśākhā. Viśākhā on Āṣāḍha śukla 10 is astronomically plausible.
as_written extended to the end of the date verse; notes expanded.

date.as_written: sataddevatsare pūrṇṇa paścāvaśām ekādhike tadā āśāmāśe śukladaśaṃyāṃ tithim uttamaṃ viśākhaṛkṣaṃ nāme tu

notes: The colophon names no persons: no scribe, patron, owner or king. The date verse is corrupt. 'sataddevatsare pūrṇṇa paścāvaśām ekādhike' most likely stands for 'śatadve vatsare pūrṇe pañcāśad ekādhike', meaning 'when 200 years were complete, plus fifty-one', i.e. year 251. The catalogue gives [NS] 200, which apparently ignores 'pañcāśad ekādhike'. The year should be checked against the manuscript image. The era is not written; NS is assumed from the Newari script and the Nepalese provenance. If the year is 251, NS 251 is about 1131 CE; if 200, about 1080 CE. 'āśāmāśe' = āṣāḍhamāse. Moon in Viśākhā on Āṣāḍha śukla 10 is astronomically plausible. The closing words 'likhitaṃ sārasaṃgrahakubjikā' give a title for the text ('Sārasaṃgraha-Kubjikā'), not a person.
